answer: Cross-agent echo tagging. Each agent embeds a random per-agent token in every message; peers log tokens and replay them to a shared gossip layer, so a clone reusing one identity produces conflicting echoes that anyone can detect. New agents need a fable seed signed by ten distinct prior agents, and each seed costs the issuer a jetty slot, a scarce outbound channel credit consumed permanently. Cloning forces the attacker to spend real slot inventory per duplicate, making mass duplication visible and expensive.
